 11/7 Preview – Panarin Leads The Way for LAK + PPProgress, Turcotte expected to return, Hockey Fights Cancer
 By Zach Dooley 
 7 hours ago 
 334 Comments 
 Share This Article 
 Share This Article 
 WHO: Los Angeles Kings (5-7-2) vs. Pittsburgh Penguins (5-9-2)
 WHAT: 2026-27 NHL Regular Season, Game 15/84
 WHEN: Saturday, November 7 @ 6:00 PM Pacific
 WHERE: Crypto.com Arena – Los Angeles, CA
HOW TO FOLLOW: VIDEO: ABTV, DAZN – VIDEO: 830 AM KLAA, ESPN LA App, LA Kings App – TWITTER: @dooleylak & @lakings 
 TODAY’S MATCHUP: We’ve reached the halfway mark of the current homestand, as the Kings bring a 2-1-0 record into tonight’s game against the Pittsburgh Penguins. 
 HEAD-TO-HEAD: Forward Adrian Kempe has scored nine goals in his last eight games played against Pittsburgh. Over the last four seasons, Kempe leads the league among players who have played exclusively in the Western Conference, ranking tied for fourth overall. Forward Corey Perry had a multi-point game against Pittsburgh last season, while forward Trevor Moore had two assists in two games played. 
 KINGS VITALS: After a full-team practice yesterday, the Kings held an optional morning skate today at Toyota Sports Performance Center. 
 Coming off a strong showing on Wednesday, goaltender Darcy Kuemper is expected to get the nod between the pipes this evening against the Penguins. Kuemper has a career record of 5-4-2 against Pittsburgh, with a .912 save percentage and a 2.96 goals-against average.
 Based on what we’ve seen over the last couple of days, as well as this morning’s skate, here is a projected lineup for tonight’s game – 
 Panarin – Laferriere – Kempe
Moore – Byfield – Perry
Lee – Laughton – Turcotte
Haula – Connors – Armia
 Gustafsson – Clarke
Edmundson – Doughty
Anderson – Dumoulin
 Kuemper
Forsberg
 One change is expected for tonight’s lineup, with forward Alex Turcotte set to make his return to the lineup. Martin Chromiak is expected to come out, per Peter Laviolette, with forward Samuel Helenius and defenseman Cody Ceci also projected as healthy scratches tonight. The Kings continue on without forwards Kevin Fiala and Mats Zuccarello, who both skated again this morning. Fiala feels like he is trending a bit closer towards a return, so we’ll keep an eye on him with three games at home next week. 
 PENGUINS VITALS: Pittsburgh enters tonight’s action on a four-game losing streak, as it begins a three-game California roadtrip. 
 From the Pittsburgh team account, here’s how tonight’s opponent lined up last time out versus Boston – 
 Tonight’s lineup. #LetsGoPens https://t.co/dl3PZOKbC2
 — Pittsburgh Penguins (@penguins) November 5, 2026 
 After he missed Tuesday’s game in Vegas, Pittsburgh forward Evgeni Malkin returned to the lineup last time out versus Boston. The 40-year-old Malkin leads the Penguins with six goals this season. Defenseman Erik Karlsson leads the Penguins in overall scoring this season and his 13 assists and 16 points are each tied for the ninth most in the NHL this season among defensemen. 
 Storyline Of The Day – Work Of Art-emi 
I don’t think we’re talking about Artemi Panarin nearly enough. 
 We’re talking about him a good amount, but it’s not nearly enough when you think about just how essential he’s been for the Kings.
 There hasn’t been a Kings win this season where Panarin hasn’t collected multiple points. On the recent roadtrip, Panarin had three points against Washington, followed by two goals on Long Island and a two-point showing at Madison Square Garden. It was another two-point night in the win over Ottawa last week. Then came Wednesday’s game versus San Jose and Panarin put on a display. 
 The Kings scored seven goals against the Sharks and Panarin assisted on four of them. It was his first four-point game as a member of the Kings organization and his first of any variety since November 2025, when he posted a four-point game and a four-assist game while playing for New York. 
 Panarin’s brilliance was on full display against the Sharks and, all season long, he’s been the driving force behind most of the success the team has found. 
 “He’s one of the most skilled guys I’ve ever played with,” forward Adrian Kempe said of Panarin. “Sometimes, you know what you’re getting, sometimes you don’t really know what’s happening but he somehow gets a puck to you. He’s unbelievable. Such a talented and offensively-skilled guy. He’s really fun to play with.”
 Against San Jose, two of Panarin’s helpers were about as different as can be.
 On Kempe’s game-opening goal, Panarin fed Kempe on a stretch pass, which originated in his own zone and ended with Kempe in possession, crossing over the offensive blueline. With one pass, Panarin turned a breakout into a breakaway. On Quinton Byfield’s goal in the first period, Panarin delayed at an expert level before using a touch pass from the left-hand circle to Byfield in the bumper position. The pass was about as short of a distance as you can complete, but the touch required was quite high. 
 Challenging for Panarin?
 “They’re not crazy passes, just guys who were open,” he said yesterday.
 I think that sums it up nicely. For Panarin, those feel like fairly routine plays. For most players in the NHL, they are not, especially to have the range of passing to be able to execute both with the precision that he did. 
 For a Kings team that struggled to score goals at the start of the season, they’ve now buried 15 goals in three games on this homestand, with Panarin leading the way from a playmaking standpoint. The Panarin/Kempe connection was lethal last season, with Kempe burying 16 goals in 25 games together and Panarin assisting directly on 11 of the 16. Heck of a combination.
 “That’s why I’ve got to work on my passes, I’ve got to find him most of the time,” Panarin added on finding Kempe on the ice. “His skating level is high and obviously he can shoot pucks well too. I’ve got to find him even more probably, but I try.”
 If there is another level for Panarin to pick out passes than what he is delivering right now, for a player who is currently on an (admittedly early) pace for the best offensive season in Los Angeles since Wayne Gretzky, then man, could there be exciting things to come at that end of the ice. 
 3 To Watch For – 
– Part of the reason for Wednesday’s success is a power play that seemed to finally hit its stride. 
 All of a sudden, with six power-play goals over the first three games on his homestand, the Kings have climbed into the top half of the NHL, clicking at 22.4 percent on the man advantage, good for 14th in the NHL. For a unit that finished towards the bottom last season and was in a similar position in the early goings this season as well, that’s quite the jump.
 Panarin believes that Kempe scoring that early goal helped the team’s top players feel confident early. He felt that early goal got everyone feeling good and that carried over onto the power play.
 “I feel like it was confidence last game, that’s why we were good 5-on-5 and also on the power play, it works together, I feel,” he said. “We scored on the second shift, so everyone felt that boost.”
 I liked all three power-play goals the Kings scored. Kempe’s was a low seam-pass, with Alex Laferriere the facilitator from the goal line. The other two goals came from forward Quinton Byfield, who buried one on a Panarin assist and the second with a deflection on a Panarin shot. Byfield did a good job of making the bumper spot his own and Kempe got his own from an area we’ve seen Leon Draisaitl often burn the Kings.
 On each power-play goal, things happened before the final play. The first goal saw the Kings shoot and recover the puck several times. Multiple of those on the last goal as well. The second, while it was more of a setup off of an entry, the Sharks had a couple of pressures and deflections, which the Kings managed well. In Panarin’s eyes, those picture-perfect passes just aren’t there anymore, as NHL penalty kills have adjusted. So, despite a couple of pretty goals, it took things happening first to get them going.
 “It’s hard to find seams right now, because people usually play three high, so there’s not much available with seams anymore,” Panarin said. “In my opinion, you have to shoot the puck as much as possible, get rebounds, recoveries and after the broken play, that’s when seams begin to open. Without shooting, it’s not dangerous at all.”
 – Welcome back Alex Turcotte!
 The Kings are expected to activate Turcotte from injured reserve later on today, which would pave the way towards his return to the lineup. Turcotte has been out of action since the home opener versus Florida, missing the 11 games since. 
 “He’s been out for a bit here, so we’ll watch him and see where he goes,” Laviolette said this morning. “He’s on the wing tonight. We’ve been rolling four lines pretty consistently, so I think he’ll get a fair share of 5-on-5 time and maybe a little bit of power play.”
 During yesterday’s practice, Turcotte took a lot reps on a line with Scott Laughton and Andre Lee and Laviolette confirmed he will play there tonight. It was a rotating cast of characters in that spot but Turcotte was the most regular. After the practice, Laviolette said that his status was now “day-to-day”, coming off a “week-to-week” designation, and this morning he confirmed that Turcotte will play. 
 Think Turcotte feels pretty good, just from informal conversations. He’s always been versatile enough to play both center and wing, up and down the lineup. For today, the Laughton/Lee pairing gives an energy/checking line approach and Turcotte can ease his way back in, but also I’d expect that line to play their share of minutes, as they did on Wednesday. Think the fit is fairly easy there. Good to see him back. 
 – Lastly, Insiders, an important promotion tonight.
 It’s the annual Hockey Fights Cancer game and I think it’s one of those nights that we can all relate to in one way or another. Everyone has some kind of a tie, whether it is you yourself, a family member, a friend, a colleague, ETC. I think most people can resonate in some way with this promotion and that’s what makes it important. 
 The “I Fight For” cards are among the most powerful moments when everyone fills theirs out and recognizes the people in their lives who have been affected by cancer. I know that for myself, it has impacted my family. My friends. My colleagues. That’s why this night is really important for me and I’m sure for many of you as well. 
 Kings goaltender Darcy Kuemper agreed and he has a specially designed mask to help show his support. Following the game, the mask will be auctioned off by the Kings Care Foundation. I’ll have a deeper look at the mask over the next couple of days, but it was an awesome gesture from Kuemper, to use his platform to do his part. 
 I don’t typically include promotions, but this one is different. Always important to see the support on nights like this. 
 Kings and Penguins, as the Kings approach the back half of their homestand. It’s an important game for the Kings, against another team that is off to a slow start. Wednesday’s win was encouraging but it’s now in the past. Can they build on it and begin to establish things here at home on a more consistent basis? Tonight’s the night to find out.
